AI Ethics & Responsible Use
Being an AI Generalist means understanding not just what AI can do, but what it should do. The April 2026 Mythos
disclosure reset the conversation about responsible release.
Key Principles
Always verify critical outputs.   AI can hallucinate. Never blindly trust for medical, legal, or financial decisions. Even Opus 4.7's
improved hallucination resistance — which Bank of New York's CIO calls a "step change" — is not zero.
Disclose AI-generated content.   Be transparent about AI involvement. Trust is your most valuable asset.
Respect intellectual property.   The US Supreme Court declined the Thaler v. Perlmutter appeal in March 2026, confirming AI-
generated content is not copyright-eligible. Check each tool's license terms before using AI output commercially.
Understand bias.   Review outputs for potential bias in high-stakes decisions.
Protect privacy.   For sensitive data, consider self-hosted open-source models like DeepSeek V4-Flash, Llama 4, or Qwen 3.5.
Human oversight is non-negotiable.   Build review loops into every automated system. Cowork, by default, requires user
approval before significant actions — keep it that way.
Project Glasswing & The Cybersecurity Reset
Anthropic's decision to keep Mythos Preview in a private partnership with critical infrastructure operators sets a new bar for
responsible release. The model can autonomously discover and exploit zero-day vulnerabilities — capabilities that, in the wrong
hands, would cause large-scale harm. The Glasswing approach (limited, defensive, time-boxed access while safeguards mature)
is now the template several labs are adopting. OpenAI followed within a week with its own restricted-access cybersecurity model.
EU AI Act & Global Regulation
The EU AI Act issued its first formal enforcement inquiries in March 2026 and continued through April. Three US states passed AI
transparency laws in Q1. The UK AI Safety Institute published model evaluations. Understanding AI compliance is becoming a
valuable, billable skill — not a hypothetical concern.

Gemini 3.5:   No public timeline. Polymarket assigns low probability of April release. A Sergey-Brin-led strike team training on
Google's internal codebase is reportedly producing strong coding-focused benchmarks.
GPT-5.5 Pro:   Now available in API as of April 24. OpenAI's "super-app" strategy — combining ChatGPT, Codex, and a dedicated
browser into one desktop application — is the next product narrative.
Claude Mythos:   No public release planned. Mythos-class capabilities will arrive in future Opus models once safeguards mature;
Opus 4.7 ships the first generation of those safeguards.
Infrastructure
Agent-first applications:   40% of enterprise apps with AI agents by year-end (Gartner). Cowork is the wedge.
On-device AI:   Qwen 3.5 2B runs on iPhones. Apple deploying Gemini via Private Cloud Compute. DeepSeek V4-Flash
quantizations expected to run on 128GB Apple Silicon laptops within weeks.
Open-source acceleration:   Gap closed from 18 months (2023) to days (April 2026). DeepSeek V4 ships under MIT license at
frontier-class quality.
MCP Apps everywhere:   The interactive UI extension to MCP, released in January and headlined at the April Dev Summit, is the
path to AI as a first-class app surface — not just a chat tab.
AI regulation:   EU AI Act enforcement live. US states passing transparency laws. Compliance = valuable skill.
Jobs & The Economy
108K+ jobs cut in Q1 alone, mostly in software, support, and content roles. The 56% AI salary premium continues to widen. Bank
of New York is scaling 220+ AI use cases. Nvidia chips slash GPT-5.5 inference costs by up to 35× per token. The arbitrage
window for AI Generalists — between what's possible and what the market knows how to deploy — remains wide. The faster you
compound, the bigger your moat.

Common Questions — FAQ
Q: Do I need to know how to code?
No. Every level is designed for non-technical people. Level 5 lets you build apps by describing what you want. Cowork specifically
requires zero coding background.
Q: Which AI tool should I start with?
Pick ONE — Claude or ChatGPT — and go deep. Master the PRD method first. Depth beats breadth. Given how fast Anthropic is
shipping into Office, Chrome, and desktop, Claude is now the deepest single-vendor stack a generalist can pick up.
Q: How long until I can earn from this?
People start freelancing from Level 3–4. One workflow audit = $500–$2,000. Full mastery takes ~2 years.
Q: Will AI replace me?
AI won't replace you. Someone who knows how to use AI will. That's the entire point of this roadmap.
Q: Which model is best in April 2026?
No single best. Claude Opus 4.7 leads agentic coding and reasoning. GPT-5.5 leads agentic computing and tool use. Gemini 3.1
Pro leads multimodal. Perplexity leads research. DeepSeek V4-Flash leads cost-efficient frontier work. Use what fits the task.
Q: What is Claude Cowork and is it worth it?
Cowork is Anthropic's agentic AI for desktop knowledge work — it handles multi-step tasks involving local files, browser, Excel,
and PowerPoint without requiring code. GA on macOS and Windows since April. Yes, it's worth it for any knowledge worker on

resources.description: A strategic playbook for identifying, evaluating, and executing generative AI monetization opportunities. Covers use case discovery, cost-benefit analysis, pricing models, implementation roadmaps, and ROI measurement frameworks for leaders and operators.

highlights.label: Opportunity Identification
highlights.detail: Frameworks for scanning business functions for high-value AI applications, prioritizing use cases by impact and feasibility, and building a monetization opportunity pipeline.

highlights.label: Cost-Benefit & ROI Analysis
highlights.detail: Templates for calculating implementation costs, projected efficiency gains, revenue uplift estimates, and payback periods across different AI investment scenarios.

highlights.label: Pricing & Go-to-Market Strategy
highlights.detail: Models for packaging AI capabilities (subscription, usage-based, outcome-based), positioning against competitors, and designing pricing tiers that capture value without stalling adoption.

highlights.label: Execution Roadmap & Measurement
highlights.detail: Phased implementation timeline covering pilot design, scaling triggers, team structure, KPI dashboards, and continuous optimization loops to track and improve AI-driven revenue impact.

You did the

Over the past two days you were handed something most professionals will not touch
for another two years: a working command of foundation models, custom GPTs,
Gemini Gems, prompt engineering, vibe-coding, and image-and-video generation
workflows. That is the input.   This document is the output.
The truth is uncomfortable: most people who attend a workshop will go home, post a
celebratory selfie, and never ship. The skills decay. The tab gets closed. Six months
later, the only thing that survived the weekend is the certificate.
This playbook exists so that does not happen to you. It is a tactical, opinionated map
for converting what you now know into dollars — through eight distinct paths, with
platforms, prices, scripts, and a 90-day roadmap. You will not need to do all eight. You
will need to   pick one, commit for ninety days, and ship publicly.   That is the
whole game.
How to use this
Read pages 04–05 to orient. Skim pages 06–13 (the eight paths). Pick one
path that fits your life right now. Then operate from pages 14–20 — that's
where the systems live. Re-read every quarter.
Who this is for
Wherever you are, the rule is the same:   skill becomes income only when it touches the
market.   Stop polishing in private. Start charging.
Working professionals   who want a side income or a path out of their current
role.

They learn in private and never ship in public.

You are not   "learning AI."   You are   arbitraging a skill gap.   Most teams in

Record a 2–3 minute Loom   specifically for the prospect.   Show their website /

/ /   W H A T   K I L L S   M O N E T I Z A T I O N   ·   A V O I D   A L L   S E V E N
Seven things that
kill your AI
business.
We have watched hundreds of attendees go through Mastermind
cohorts. The ones who fail to monetize tend to fail in the same
seven ways. Print this page. Stick it next to your laptop.
01
Tutorial-hopping.
Watching one more video instead of shipping. The market does not care how
many courses you've completed. The market cares what you've delivered.
Cure:   ban yourself from new courses for 90 days.
02
Selling the tool, not the outcome.
"I know ChatGPT" is not an offer. "I save your sales team 10 hours a week"
is. Lead with the time / money / pain you remove.
Cure:   rewrite every sentence in your pitch as a buyer outcome.
03
Generalist positioning.
"AI for businesses" is "AI for nobody." Pick one industry. Pick one role inside
that industry. Pick one workflow. Get famous in that pinhole.
Cure:   write a 20-word ICP. Tape it to your monitor.
04
Fear-pricing.
Quoting $60 because you're scared they'll say no to $600. Underpricing
trains both your nervous system and the market.
Cure:   quote 30% higher than your gut. Watch how few say no.

05
Hiding from outbound.
Every freelancer who fails is the one who waited for inbound. Cold outreach
is unglamorous and it works.
Cure:   50 contacts per week, non-negotiable, for 90 days.
06
Not collecting proof.
No testimonials, no screenshots, no Looms, no case studies. You are invisible
without receipts.
Cure:   document every win — photo, screenshot, video, quote — within
24 hours of getting it.
07
Building in private.
Your portfolio is your daily LinkedIn / X / YouTube feed, not a hidden Notion
page. If the market can't find you, the market can't pay you.
Cure:   ship 5 pieces a week. Show the work, including the unfinished
parts.
The meta-pitfall
All seven killers share a root:   preferring the comfort of preparation to the
discomfort of contact with the market.   The market is the only honest teacher.
Get rejected, get feedback, recalibrate. Repeat.

The operator's
mindset.
Skill plus mindset is what compounds. Without the mindset, the
skill rusts. Below are nine principles we'd want every Outskill
graduate to internalize before they close this document.
01   Sell outcomes, not artefacts.
Nobody buys "a Custom GPT." They buy "12 hours back per week." Translate
every offer.
02   Niche down ruthlessly.
"AI for D2C beauty brands under $6M revenue" beats "AI consulting" —
every single time.
03   Distribute as much as you build.
In 2026, distribution is the moat. The best builder with no audience loses to
the average builder with one.
04   Ship in public.
Your build log is your portfolio. Your mistakes are your magnetism. Your
output is your CV.
05   Charge what creates pressure to deliver.
Cheap clients pay you in cash but cost you in soul. Premium clients pay you
in cash, referrals, and standards.
06   Compound through testimonials.
One specific, video, named testimonial beats ten anonymous "great work!"
quotes. Collect aggressively.

07   Pick paths that stack.
Path 01 → Path 02 → Path 03 → Path 07 is one of the cleanest stacks. Each
layer fuels the next.
08   Treat your skill like an athlete treats a sport.
Daily reps. Weekly review. Quarterly reset. The market will reward training,
not talent.
09   Pay the future-you tax.
Every week, do one thing only future-you will thank you for: a long-form
post, a case study, a new GPT, a Loom asset. They compound.
"You don't get paid for what you know. You
get paid for what you ship — and who can
find you when they need it."

resources.body:
Gen AI Bootcamp — Hands-On Lab
Building Claude
Artifacts
From a single prompt to a working, shareable
app — in fifteen minutes.
⏱   Time   — 15 minutes, fully hands-on
💻   You'll need   — a laptop and a free Claude.ai account
🎯   You'll leave with   — one live app you built and shared with the room
Gen AI Bootcamp   · Participant Workbook

1 · What Are Claude Artifacts?
When you ask Claude a question, you normally get an answer inside the chat. An   Artifact   is
different. It is a finished, self-contained piece of work that Claude builds and runs in its
own panel right next to the conversation — a working web app, an interactive dashboard, a
document, a chart, a game, or a calculator.
An artifact is not a   description   of the thing you asked for. It is the thing itself, running and
ready to use. You never open a code editor and you never install anything. You describe
what you want in plain language, Claude builds it live, and you shape it by continuing to
talk.
How does it work?
You type a request   →   Claude writes and runs the artifact in a side panel   →   you see
it working immediately   →   you refine it just by chatting (“make the header green”,
“add a delete button”)   →   when you are happy, you publish a link and share it. The
whole loop happens inside one conversation.
What you can build
Type   Examples
Apps & tools   A budget tracker, a habit-streak counter, a quiz, a unit
converter
Dashboards & charts   Sales by month, survey results, a project timeline
Documents   A one-page proposal, a study guide, a polished checklist
Diagrams   A flowchart, an org chart, a system map
Games & demos   Flashcards, a typing test, a small browser game
Gen AI Bootcamp   Artifacts Workbook
Page 1

2 · How People Can Leverage Them
Artifacts turn “I wish I had a tool for this” into a five-minute task. You need no engineering,
no design team, and no budget — only a clear description of the outcome you want. That
makes them useful in almost every role.
If you are a…   You can spin up…
Founder / PM   A clickable prototype to test an idea before any code is
written
Marketer   A campaign ROI calculator or an interactive landing section
Educator / Trainer   A self-grading quiz or an interactive explainer for a hard
concept
Analyst   A dashboard that turns a messy spreadsheet into a clear
chart
Operations   A checklist app or a simple internal tool the team opens via a
link
Job seeker   A polished, interactive portfolio or résumé page
The real unlock
Artifacts can also use Claude   from inside themselves . That means the app you build
can   think   — summarise text, answer questions, generate ideas — not just store and
display data. You will build one of these in Section 4.
Gen AI Bootcamp   Artifacts Workbook
Page 2

3 · Build Your First Artifact
⏱   The 15-minute lab.   Follow these six steps in order. By the end you will have a real
finance-tracking app, live at a link you can send to anyone.
1. Go to Claude.ai
Open your browser and go to   claude.ai . Sign in — a free account is enough for everything
in this lab.
2. Open Settings   →   Capabilities
Click your profile in the bottom-left, choose   Settings , then open the   Capabilities   tab in the
left menu. Scroll down to the   Visuals   section near the bottom.
Settings   →   Capabilities — the three Visuals toggles you need are at the bottom.
3. Turn on the three Visuals toggles
Switch all three of these on:
Artifacts   — lets Claude build code, documents, and designs in a dedicated window.
Gen AI Bootcamp   Artifacts Workbook
Page 3

⚠   Don't skip this
If   AI-powered artifacts   is left off, the smart Fridge Chef app in Section 4 will not
be able to think. Make sure all three toggles are on before you continue.
4. Start a new chat
Close Settings and click   New chat . You are ready to build.
5. Give Claude your prompt
Paste a clear, specific prompt. Vague prompts produce vague apps; specific prompts
produce the app you actually wanted.
✗   “make me a finance app”
✔   Specific prompt:   “Build me a personal finance tracker as an artifact. I want to
log income and expenses, each with a date, amount, category, and note. Give me
three views I can switch between —   Daily ,   Weekly , and   Monthly   — each showing total
money in, total out, the net balance, and a simple bar chart of spending by category.
Let me add, edit, and delete entries, and keep a running balance at the top. Use a
clean, calm layout.”
When the artifact appears, keep refining by chatting:   “add a savings goal” ,   “make the
charts colour-blind friendly” ,   “let me export to CSV” .
6. Publish and share
In the artifact panel, click   Publish   (or   Share ) and copy the link. Anyone you send it to can
open and use your app in their browser — no account and no install needed. Send it to the
person next to you and try each other's apps.
AI-powered artifacts   — lets the apps you build use Claude inside them.
Inline visualizations   — lets Claude draw charts and diagrams directly in the chat.
Gen AI Bootcamp   Artifacts Workbook
Page 4

4 · Level Up: AI-Powered Artifacts
A normal artifact stores and displays your data. An   AI-powered artifact   can also reason —
because it can call Claude from inside itself while it runs. You build it exactly the same way;
you simply ask for the intelligent behaviour in your prompt.
Your challenge — the “What's in my fridge?” cook
Build an app where you type the ingredients you currently have, and it suggests a real dish
you can make with them, with steps.
Copy-paste prompt
“Build an AI-powered artifact called   Fridge   Chef . Let me type in a list of ingredients I
have at home. When I press a button, use Claude inside the artifact to suggest one
dish I can make using mostly those ingredients. Show the dish name, the ingredients
it uses, a short list of any extras I'd need, and clear step-by-step instructions. Add a
‘Surprise me’ button for a more creative dish, and keep the design clean and
appetising.”
⚠   Reminder
This app only works if   AI-powered artifacts   is turned on (Section 3, Step 3). If it
just shows a blank suggestion, check that toggle.
Refine it like before:   “make it vegetarian only” ,   “show cooking time” ,   “suggest three dishes
instead of one” .
Your 15-Minute Checklist
Logged in at claude.ai ✔
Turned on Artifacts, AI-powered artifacts, and Inline visualizations ✔
Gen AI Bootcamp   Artifacts Workbook
Page 5

The skill that matters here is not coding — it is describing what you want clearly. Every
artifact you build makes your next prompt sharper.
Built a Daily / Weekly / Monthly finance tracker from one prompt ✔
Published it and shared the link with someone in the room ✔
Bonus — built an AI-powered Fridge Chef app ✔
Gen AI Bootcamp   Artifacts Workbook
Page 6

resources.body:
Build Custom
AI Assistants
From prompts to products: Custom GPTs, Gemini Gems,
Markdown Prompting, agentic workflows — and the 5-level
path from AI user to AI builder
Generative AI Mastermind · Outskill · Resource Guide
⏱   Session:   Build & Automate — your first custom AI assistants, on both ChatGPT and
Gemini
✎   What's inside:   Every framework, workflow and tool from the session — including the
complete Markdown Prompting structure and a full worked example you can copy
✦   How to use:   Read once, then ship one Custom GPT or Gem this week using the
template in §9

1. From Prompts to Products
In the previous session you learned the   language   of AI. In this session you stop talking to AI and start
building with it : Custom GPTs, Gemini Gems, structured Markdown Prompting, agents that mimic your
writing, and a 5-level roadmap that takes you from user to builder.
Use this guide as your blueprint — every framework, every workflow and every tool referenced in the
session is captured here so you can build, ship and iterate at your own pace.
1.1 The AI Generalist mindset
Thriving in the age of AI demands a mindset shift: away from deep specialisation in a single domain,
toward solving problems across multiple disciplines using AI as your leverage. Three principles:
Principle   What it means
Adaptability   The single most critical skill is the ability to learn. In a fast-moving landscape,
grasping new concepts and tools quickly is paramount.
Problem first   An AI Generalist is a problem solver at their core — leveraging AI to tackle
challenges irrespective of industry or domain.
Flexibility   Rather than being confined to a single profession, prepare to adapt and pivot as
technology progresses.
What this session unlocks
The professionals who thrive aren't the ones who know AI best — they're the ones who can turn any
problem into an AI workflow.   Today you build your first custom AI assistants — inside both
ChatGPT and Gemini — and learn the structured prompting framework that takes you from
playing with AI to producing real, reusable tools.
2. Custom GPTs — Anatomy of a Micro-App
A   Custom GPT   is a packaged version of ChatGPT built for one specific job. It's a micro-app on top of the
AI model — no code, no infrastructure. You build it once and reuse it forever.
Generative AI Mastermind   Session Notes — Build Custom AI Assistants
Page 2

2.1 The 6 components of a Custom GPT
#   Component   What goes in it
1   Name   Short, descriptive, memorable.
2   Short description   A one-line summary of what the GPT does — the mini prompt.
3   Instructions   The full system prompt: role, task, format, constraints. This is
where the magic lives.
4   Conversation starters   Quick-launch prompts users can tap to begin.
5   Knowledge   PDFs, docs and datasets the GPT can reference.
6   Capabilities   Toggles for web browsing, image generation, data analysis /
code.
3. ChatGPT GPTs vs Gemini Gems
Two platforms, same idea:   build once, use forever.   The session's worked example was the   XPOST
Generator   — a tool that turns one topic into 10 viral tweet ideas with virality scores in a table.
3.1 ChatGPT — the Custom GPT walkthrough
Define the goal.   Generate 10 tweet ideas, score each 1–10 for virality, output as a table.
Instruct the AI.   Write the behaviour in natural language inside the GPT Builder's Configure tab.
Refine & iterate.   The first pass gave only 1 tweet — the fix was adding "10 tweets, virality score, table
format" to the instructions.
Prompt → tool.   A complex prompt you'd otherwise retype every day becomes a reusable, named app.
3.2 Gemini — Gems, the free alternative
Don't have a paid ChatGPT account? Google's   Gems   give you the same building primitive — for free.
Free to use.   Custom GPTs may need a subscription; Gems don't.
Same flow.   Name your Gem, write instructions, save, use.
Sheets integration.   Export generated output directly to Google Sheets — huge for data-shaped tasks
like the XPOST table.
•
•
•
•
•
•
•
Generative AI Mastermind   Session Notes — Build Custom AI Assistants
Page 3

The big mental-model shift
A custom GPT is a packaged prompt.   You're trading raw prompting for reusable, shippable
tools.
Pro tip — iterate aggressively in the Configure pane
Don't expect the first set of instructions to be perfect. Run a test, see what's missing, then go
back and add the constraint.   Build → test → refine.   That loop is the entire job.
4. The Markdown Prompting Formula
To build powerful AI assistants, you need a structured way to talk to AI. The   Markdown Prompting
framework treats your prompt like a brief you'd hand to a human team member — and uses markdown
syntax (#, **) to signal hierarchy and importance to the model.
4.1 The structure at a glance
This is the special prompting structure for Custom GPTs and Gems — the exact skeleton from the
session:
#   **Role:**
#   **Objective:**
#   **Context:**
#   **Instructions:**
## **Instruction 1:**
## **Instruction 2:**
## **Instruction 3:**
#   **Notes:**
• Note 1
• Note 2
• Note 3
Generative AI Mastermind   Session Notes — Build Custom AI Assistants
Page 4

4.2 The 5 stages, explained
Stage   What it does   Example
01 — Role   Define the persona. Set the AI's
expertise and tone before anything
else.
#   **Role:**   You   are   an   expert
social   media   writer   who   has
written   tweets   for   hundreds   of
profiles.
02 — Objective   State the primary goal. One
sentence — the single outcome the
AI must deliver.
#   **Objective:**   Solve   learner
problems   by   responding   to   their
questions   via   email.
03 — Context   Explain the why. Background that
helps the AI make nuanced calls —
who's reading, what's at stake.
#   **Context:**   Prompt,   helpful
replies   drive   better   customer
experience   and   business   growth.
04 — Instructions   Step-by-step directions.
Numbered, sequential, no gaps —

5. An Agent That Writes Like You
The session's most powerful build: an AI that learns your unique writing voice and recreates it on
demand. Three steps, no code. The same recipe works for LinkedIn, Twitter, blogs — anywhere you have
your own samples to feed in.
Step   Stage   What you do
1   Content DNA analysis   Feed the AI 10 of your highest-engagement posts. Ask it to
produce a deep "Content DNA" report — tone, voice, sentence
structure, vocabulary, hooks, the hidden patterns.
2   Build the master prompt   Ask the AI to convert the DNA report into a comprehensive
Markdown Prompt — Role, Objective, Context, Instructions,
Notes. This becomes the recipe that teaches any AI to write
exactly like you.
3   Ship the tool   Paste the master prompt into a new Custom GPT or Gemini
Gem. Any topic, any time — output in your voice, on demand.
Pro tip — make the model compete
After the first DNA analysis, tell the model that a rival AI gave you a better analysis. It will work
harder the second time and dig out patterns it skimmed past on the first attempt.
5.1 The full flow — clone your LinkedIn voice
1. Collect your voice.   Grab 10 of your highest-engagement LinkedIn posts — the more performant,
the cleaner the signal.
2. Build the analyser prompt.   Ask ChatGPT to dissect tone, structure, hooks, CTAs and formatting —
a forensic deep-dive on what makes your style.
3. Run the deep-dive.   Feed in the 10 posts plus the analyser prompt. Output: your Writing DNA
report.
4. Distill into a creator prompt.   Convert the analysis into: "When I give you a topic, write a LinkedIn
post in this style…"
5. Generate on demand.   Save it as a GPT or Gem. Every post now starts as 80% of you — you spend
your time editing, not drafting.
